newsitem.title: UK: Conservatives face disaster in Scotland, polls say.
newsitem.headline: Conservatives face disaster in Scotland, polls say.

text.p: EDINBURGH, April 27 (REUTER) - Britain's ruling Conservatives could be almost wiped out in Scotland in the May 1 general election, opinion polls published on Sunday said.
An NOP poll in Scotland for the Sunday Times newspaper suggested that the Conservatives would retain only two of the 10 Scottish seats they held in the outgoing parliament.
The poll, carried out last Friday, showed Tony Blair's opposition Labour Party up two points in a week to 49 percent, while the Conservatives dropped one to 14 percent.
The Scottish National Party (SNP) dropped four points to 24 percent and the Liberal Democrats gained four to 12 percent.
An ICM poll for Scotland on Sunday said telephone surveys in key Scottish constituencies indicated that three of Prime Minister John Major's top ministers would lose their seats on Thursday.

It said Foreign Minister Malcolm Rifkind was trailing Labour in Edinburgh Pentlands, Scottish Secretary Michael Forsyth was down on Labour in Stirling and Trade Secretary Ian Lang would lose to the SNP in Galloway and Upper Nithsdale.
ICM carried out a random sample of 707 voters in Pentlands, 702 in Stirling and 708 in Galloway between April 21 and 26.
